newsitem.title: BELGIUM: GBL, Electrafina will not merge - Frere.
newsitem.headline: GBL, Electrafina will not merge - Frere.

text.p: Belgian financier Albert Frere, chairman of Belgian holding company Electrafina, told shareholders on Tuesday that there was no plan to merge Electrafina with its parent company GBL.

"We have considered a merger of GBL and Electrafina, but the issue is not the order of the day right now," Electrafina chairman Frere said in reply to a question at the annual meeting of Electrafina shareholders.

He said the GBL/Electrafina group only had a limited number of strategic assets and a merger would not improve clarity or decision-making. A merger would however reduce the group's choice of partners and financing.
He said that for instance Compagnie Generale des Eaux (CGE), which has 22.5 percent in Electrafina, was interested in Electrafina, but not in GBL.
"CGE has no interest in (GBL units) BBL or Royale Belge, that is why we must keep Electrafina and GBL separate," Frere said.
At the end of 1996 GBL had a 49.2 percent stake in Electrafina. Among Electrafina's key assets are stakes in PetroFina, Audiofina and Suez.
